matters.title: Council action is requested to issue a purchase order to Burns & McDonnell (B&M) in the amount of $350,249 and to authorize change orders up to ten (10) percent of the authorized amount, for the Substation A 69kV Reconfiguration Engineer-Procure-Construct (EPC) Phase 1 services for the Power & Light Department (IPL). Approved
matters.text:
The purpose of the Substation A 69kV reconfiguration project is to replace obsolete equipment and allow for future generation. Reconfiguration of the south 69kV bus includes new bus supports and switch stands, new 69kV switches, new 69kV relay panels, and separating the 69kV north & south bus differential relays onto separate panels. 
This project will be split into two phases. The first phase will be for initial design services and the second will be for procurement and construction services. 
IPL’s intent is to complete construction during the outages for improvements under the Able Battery Generator Interconnection Agreements (GIA). While the Substation A 69kV reconfiguration will utilize this outage window, it is entirely different from the Able Battery project scope. Consequently, these costs will not be recovered through Southwest Power Pool’s (SPP) FERC-approved tariff. 
B&M is currently the EPC vendor working within Substation A and has extensive, ongoing experience with the facility during this outage timeframe. B&M has the immediate staff available to perform the EPC duties for the Substation A 69kV Reconfiguration. B&M is an approved A/E vendor, and has resources, skill sets, software, and systems in place to perform these EPC duties efficiently and economically. 
Approval of this item authorizes the Finance Director to issue change orders up to ten (10) percent of the authorized amount, providing appropriations are available.

matters.title: Council action is requested to expend $500,000 to Arkansas Electric Cooperatives for pole-mount and pad-mount transformers and to authorize change orders of up to ten percent (10%) of the authorized amount for the Power & Light Department (IPL). Approved
matters.text:
The Transmission and Distribution Division of Power and Light needs distribution transformers to maintain power distribution to customers. Arkansas Electric has a varied stock of pole and pad-mount transformers that IPL is unable to acquire without extended lead times through IPL’s contracted vendor. IPL has had a contract with Arkansas Electric in the past, and they are a known vendor that meets transformer specifications. IPL acquired a Volume Commitment Agreement for guaranteed quarterly delivery of needed transformers. Arkansas Electric's pricing is comparable to IPL’s contracted vendors. IPL is currently experiencing about an 18–24-month lead time with contracted vendors.
Approval of this item authorizes the Finance Director to issue change orders up to a total of ten (10) percent of the original authorized amount, so long as appropriations are available.

Memorandum
To: Mayor and Members of the City Council
Cc: City Manager
From: Joseph Hegendeffer, Director, Independence Power & Light
Date: 4/10/2026
Subject: Single Source Justification – Arkansas Electric Cooperative Corporation
Single Source Justification
Procurement of Distribution Transformers
Arkansas Electric Cooperative Corporation
Due to ongoing supply chain constraints and extended lead times within the electrical
equipment manufacturing industry, Independence Power & Light (IPL) conducted outreach
to multiple domestic transformer suppliers to identify vendors capable of supporting IPL’s
operational requirements for recurring quarterly deliveries of distribution transformers.
IPL’s operational needs require:
• Reliable quarterly transformer deliveries;
• Guaranteed production allocation sufficient to support system reliability and
customer growth;
• Pricing commitments tied to each scheduled delivery tranche; and
• The ability to meet accelerated delivery timelines necessary to maintain adequate
inventory levels and support ongoing construction and maintenance activities.
During the solicitation and vendor outreach process, multiple manufacturers and
distributors were contacted regarding availability, production schedules, and pricing
commitments. While several suppliers expressed general interest in providing
transformers, no other domestic supplier was willing or able to:
• Commit contractually to quarterly delivery schedules;
• Guarantee manufacturing allocation for IPL’s required delivery cadence;
• Provide firm pricing for each quarterly delivery tranche; or
• Meet IPL’s required delivery timelines.
Arkansas Electric Cooperative Corporation was the only identified American supplier
capable of meeting IPL’s required schedule and operational delivery requirements.
Arkansas Electric demonstrated the ability to provide:
• Committed quarterly deliveries;
• Production scheduling aligned with IPL inventory and construction needs;
• Pricing associated with each delivery period; and
• Delivery timelines necessary to support system reliability and avoid operational risk
associated with transformer shortages.
Failure to secure a supplier capable of meeting these requirements would expose IPL to
increased operational risk, including inadequate inventory levels, delayed service
connections, delayed replacement of failed equipment, and potential impacts to system
reliability and customer service obligations.
Based on the vendor outreach performed and the critical schedule requirements
associated with maintaining utility operations and system reliability, Arkansas Electric
Cooperative Corporation is determined to be the only responsive and responsible
American supplier capable of meeting IPL’s operational delivery requirements within the
required timeframe. Therefore, this procurement qualifies as a single source purchase.

Approved
matters.text:
During the previously approved major inspection of the J-2 combustion turbine, a misalignment in the bearings was found. This misalignment of the bearings is the root cause of the damage to the failed stage-1 (stg-1) buckets that were known to exist. Additional, unanticipated damage was found to the stage-2 (stg-2) buckets and other rotating components of the rotor that are currently being repaired by APG.
The bearing alignment is critical to maintaining the tight tolerances at high speeds that gas turbines operate under. The bearing misalignment caused rubbing between the rotating and non-rotating parts. Due to this rubbing, there was more damage than was expected from the initial borescope inspection that alerted staff to the original issues. A failure would be highly detrimental to the turbine and costly to repair. The unit operates frequently due to demand from the Southwest Power Pool (SPP) integrated market.
The additional requested work is based on the findings during the tear down of the rotor in the APG shop. This work will ensure a balanced rotor which is required for continually safe and reliable operation of the unit. The additional scope will include machining surfaces and other precision areas, as well as the replacement of hardware that had to be destroyed for the disassembly of the rotor as well as shipping.
Approval authorizes the Finance Director to approve a change order of $74,400 (including an estimated $5K for shipping) to P.O. 26001042 and to issue additional change orders up to a total of ten (10) percent of the original authorized amount, providing that appropriations are available.

Item passes 7-0
matters.text:
Inspections of the combustion turbines are performed periodically to assess the condition of the unit to meet the load demand as well as safety and reliability requirements. Identification and repair of problem areas are essential to maintain unit availability and reduce ongoing maintenance. The purpose of the major inspection is to examine all internal rotating and stationary components from the inlet of the turbine through the exhaust.
During a borescopic inspection of the turbine performed in 2024, it was recommended to replace the Stg-1 buckets that were found to have varying degrees of damage that could contribute to a failure. Failure would be highly detrimental to the turbine and costly to repair. The unit operates frequently due to demand by the Southwest Power Pool (SPP) integrated market.
The requested major rotor repair, tentatively scheduled for April 2026, is required for continual, safe and reliable operation of the unit. The major rotor repair will include offsite disassembly and inspection of all rotating components, replacing known and as-found damaged components. The rotor repair will be conducted offsite by Allied Power Group. APG is a firm that is highly recommended by other local utilities. APG can accommodate our time frame to help ensure that J-2 gets back into the SPP pool as quickly as possible to help secure our current capacity. Any emergency findings requiring repair work will be addressed separately as determined during the inspection.
Following approval, a budget transfer of $3,172,700 will be requested on a supplemental appropriation from existing capital improvement project (CIP) 202504 - Blue Valley Chimney Demolition, to a newly created CIP 202620 – J-2 Substation Inspection (Combustion Turbine) & Repair (Rotor).

matters.title: Council action is requested to issue a purchase order to GE Vernova, in the amount of $2,015,015.33, and authorizing change orders of up to ten percent (10%) of the authorized amount, for a major inspection of the J-2 substation combustion turbine for the Power & Light Department. Item passes 7-0
matters.text:
Inspections of the combustion turbines are performed periodically to assess the condition of the unit to meet the load demand. Identification and repair of problem areas are essential to maintain unit availability and reduce ongoing maintenance. The purpose of the major inspection is to examine all the internal rotating and stationary components from the inlet of the turbine through the exhaust.
The last major inspection of the J-2 combustion turbine was in 2012. A borescopic inspection on the turbine rotor performed in 2024 recommended replacing the Stg-1 buckets that were found to have varying degrees of damage that could contribute to a failure. Failure would be highly detrimental to the turbine and costly to repair. The unit operates frequently due to demand by the Southwest Power Pool (SPP) integrated market.
The requested major inspection is required for continual safe and reliable operation of the unit. A major inspection will include onsite disassembly, inspection, use of consumable materials and reassembly of the gas turbine. The inspection will be conducted onsite by GE Vernova, the original equipment manufacturer and sole source provider. 
Following approval, a budget transfer of funds of $3,172,700 will be requested on a supplemental appropriation from existing capital improvement project (CIP) 202504 - Blue Valley Chimney Demolition, to a newly created CIP 202620 – J-2 Substation Inspection (Combustion Turbine) & Repair (Rotor).

matters.text:
Relays are essential in the process of power generation. They provide protection and allow for controlling the system output utilizing lower voltage inputs. The current electromagnetic relays are of an antiquated design that does not allow for tracking and trending system issues. Consequently, the ability to utilize analytics to predict and avoid issues is unavailable. Significant diagnostic and repair time is currently spent on issues that could potentially be avoided. 
SEL generator relays will be installed by GE Vernova Technicians. GE is the original equipment manufacturer (OEM) and has experience with the software and hardware to ensure seamless integration. SEL relays are currently being utilized throughout the rest of the system. This provides the relay technicians the familiarity and experience to be self-sufficient at programming and maintaining the proposed SEL relays.
Approval authorizes the Procurement Manager to issue change orders up to ten (10) percent of the original authorized amount, providing that appropriations are available.

Located at 400 N. Kentucky Road, the Rock Creek Pump Station (RCPS) is the City’s largest pump station, responsible for conveying approximately 60% of the total flow received by the Rock Creek Treatment Facility. Flow through RCPS ranges from 4 million gallons per day (MGD) to 30 MGD, with an average of 4.6 MGD, depending on rainfall and the return of stored wastewater to the collection system.
 The station uses multiple pumps controlled by VFDs, which adjust motor speed in real time based on wastewater depth measured by radar. This dynamic control maintains appropriate wet well levels and accommodates significant flow fluctuations.

matters.title: Council action is requested to approve expenditures for a multi-year agreement for Radio System Maintenance with Motorola Solutions for the Police Department. Item passes 7-0
matters.text:
The Eastern Jackson County Radio System Maintenance Agreement is due for renewal. This renewal will be for a 5-year term and runs on a calendar-year basis. 
The City of Independence is the primary shareholder in the Eastern Jackson County (EJC) Radio System, with the City of Blue Springs and the Central Jackson County Fire Protection District (CJCFPD) as partners. This Radio System is a part of the Metropolitan Regional Radio System (MARRS) and serves the Radio Communications needs of most of the cities east of Kansas City except Lees Summit. It also serves Jackson County.
Agencies using the EJC System pay subscriber fees to the City of Independence based on the number of radios they are using. These subscriber fees offset the costs of maintaining the system.
The EJC Radio System is managed by the Independence Police Technology Unit, and all billing and payments are managed by the City of Independence Finance Department. The Police Technology Unit has reviewed this agreement to ensure it covers all the System Maintenance needs.
Motorola submits a single invoice each year for all maintenance-related costs. This invoice includes items that individual cities, and in some cases, City Departments are responsible for. These amounts are billed to the responsible agency by Finance.
Payments for this maintenance agreement are based on a formula determined by the Finance Department. The subscriber fees paid by agencies are subtracted from the total cost of maintaining the system, and the remaining portion is split among the three partner agencies. The City of Independence pays 60%, the City of Blue Springs pays 30%, and CJCFPD pays the remaining 10% of the Shared Maintenance/Upgrade costs. This formula was determined by the percentage of system equipment owned by each agency.
Each partner agency also has specific items they are exclusively responsible for, in addition to the shared common costs. The combined individual and shared costs are billed to the partner agencies by Finance.
The amount obligated to fund the maintenance is split among the City Departments, according to a formula established by the Finance Department. This includes the Subscriber Equipment maintenance costs for individual City departments, and the Maintenance/Upgrade fees for the Independence Communications Center, which are charged to the specific City Departments. 
The total cost per year is stated in the contract. The cost-sharing formula will be applied to these amounts, and the amount the City pays for Maintenance/Upgrade will stay proportional to what is paid for year one. These costs after year two are only for maintenance and upgrade support. There will be an addendum for each year after year two to cover the infrastructure replacements. During discussions for this agreement, it was determined that Motorola could not provide a fixed price for the out years for equipment they did not supply. There is too much volatility in the supply chain.
This Maintenance Agreement is essentially a renewal of the existing agreement under which the City has been operating for the last 10 years. There are a few notable additions to the renewal agreement:
Provisions have been made for infrastructure replacements, specifically generators and HVAC units. The existing units are aging out (most have been in use for more than 14 years), and parts are becoming difficult to obtain. Both Generators and HVAC have become an intensive maintenance issue in the last few years, and these are critical components of the system. All Generators and HVAC units will be replaced during the term of the agreement.
Cybersecurity monitoring has been added to the agreement. This addition includes 24/7/365 monitoring by Motorola of all networked components of the Radio System, and any intervention/remediation required in the event of a breach.
